data.one_liner: Extract locales currently defined on the device independently of app settings.
data.what_it_does: Extracts the preferred languages and current device locale data directly from the underlying operating system. It allows reading language lists as strings or Flutter Locale objects and supports per-app language preferences on Android.
use_when: You need to detect the device's system-level preferred languages and current locale.
You are implementing an in-app language picker that interacts with Android per-app language preferences.
avoid_when: You are looking for translation management, plural rules, or locale-aware formatting utilities.
Targeting Linux where standard preferred language APIs are absent and it falls back to current locale.
strengths: Supports multiple platforms including Android, iOS, web, macOS, and Linux.
Provides both string-based and Flutter Locale object return types.
weaknesses: Linux and POSIX environments lack a standard API for preferred languages, returning only the current locale.
Requires platform-specific considerations for SwiftPM on older local Xcode setups.
data.setup_notes: No complex configuration required beyond standard Flutter plugin installation. Android per-app language setting requires device support checks.
